headline.purpose: Major page sections and final calls to action.

title.purpose: Cards, notices, disclosures, and footer groups.

metadata.purpose: Compact facts and schedule dates; never action labels or paragraphs.

metric.purpose: Large pricing values and comparison figures.

step-marker.purpose: Ordered registration and hotel journey numerals.

hero-deck.purpose: Supporting hero copy beneath the main title.

lead.purpose: Prominent section introductions and supporting emphasis.

supporting.purpose: Captions, fee timing, and footer or legal support.

journey-locator.purpose: Redundant wide-desktop wayfinding with a 44px target; not the primary action-label pattern.

shadows.name: resting-card

shadows.name: interactive-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover and focus lift when motion is allowed.

shadows.name: protected-overlay
shadows.purpose: Modal separation over a dark backdrop.

shadows.name: resting-compact
shadows.purpose: Compact resting separation for small surfaces.

shadows.name: focus-within
shadows.purpose: Quiet focus-within reinforcement without a brand-colored halo.

shadows.name: button-lift
shadows.purpose: Primary-control lift on hover and focus when motion is allowed.

shadows.name: gallery-lift
shadows.purpose: Contained gallery emphasis on hover-capable devices.

shadows.name: floating-lift
shadows.purpose: Separation for the wide-desktop Back to Top control.

shadows.name: lightbox-overlay
shadows.purpose: Deep lightbox separation over its dark backdrop.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Color, border, and compact state feedback.

motion.name: image-standard
motion.purpose: Contained gallery emphasis on hover-capable devices.

motion.name: contrast-preserving
motion.value: transform only for readable scroll-linked content
motion.purpose: Scroll choreography never fades or filters text and controls below WCAG AA at an intermediate frame.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Immediate state changes with no scroll, scale, lift, or fade timing.

components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-button-primary { display:inline-flex; min-height:46px; align-items:center; justify-content:center; border:2px solid transparent; border-radius:var(--radius,8px); padding:0 16px; background:var(--lime,#8cc63f); color:var(--navy,#12314a); font:900 14px/1.2 Aptos,'Segoe UI',Arial,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; box-shadow:0 10px 22px rgba(0,0,0,.16); transition:background-color 180ms ease,border-color 180ms ease,color 180ms ease,box-shadow 180ms ease,transform 220ms ease; } .ds-button-primary:hover,.ds-button-primary:focus-visible { border-color:var(--coral,#e95f45); background:var(--deep-navy,#0b2235); color:#fff; transform:translateY(-2px); box-shadow:0 16px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.22); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--accessible-focus-coral,#cf4b36); outline-offset:3px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) { .ds-button-primary { transition:none; } .ds-button-primary:hover,.ds-button-primary:focus-visible { transform:none; } }

narrative.overview:
The experience should feel like arriving at a well-run FCI registration desk set inside the Riviera destination: unmistakably branded, calm under pressure, and warm enough to build anticipation. Operational truth leads every composition, while approved photography and the sunlit accent palette keep the page from feeling administrative.

The system pairs a structured navy frame with warm paper surfaces, decisive lime actions, accessible teal wayfinding, and restrained coral signals. Verified prior-convention and resort imagery supplies atmosphere; the interface supplies sequence, recovery, and confidence. It is a registration tool with hospitality, not a generic conference template.
keyCharacteristics: Registration-first hierarchy with fees, attendee forms, and hotel follow-through kept explicit.
Deep navy structure, warm paper reading surfaces, and rare high-energy lime actions.
Editorial serif headlines paired with a practical system sans-serif for operations.
Approved FCI, verified prior-convention, speaker, and resort assets instead of invented visual proof.
Responsive behavior that stays complete from 320px through wide desktop and at 200% reflow.
Motion that supports state but disappears cleanly when reduced motion is requested.

rules.name: The Registration Color Rule
rules.body: Lime identifies the next primary action; do not spend it on general decoration.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Warm Signal Coral marks selection and policy emphasis. Accessible Focus Coral marks focus on light surfaces; Warm Signal Coral or white may mark focus on navy and photographic surfaces.

rules.name: The Focus Contrast Rule
rules.body: A focus indicator contrasts at least 3:1 with the immediately adjacent surface and never relies on color alone.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Serif type establishes destination and occasion; sans-serif type carries every task, status, and decision.

rules.name: The Sentence Rule
rules.body: Fragments and interface labels use Title Case; complete sentences retain sentence case and normal punctuation.

rules.name: The Operational-First Rule
rules.body: Fees, role selection, registration recovery, and hotel follow-through appear before galleries or optional sponsorship details.

rules.name: The Safe-Area Rule
rules.body: Full-bleed decorative media may extend into device insets; essential text, controls, sticky navigation, dialogs, and fixed controls stay inside the safe content box.

rules.name: The Responsive Media Rule
rules.body: Routine images use responsive WebP candidates, intrinsic dimensions, and truthful sizes; full JPEGs are fallback or explicit-enlargement sources.

rules.name: The Neutral Elevation Rule
rules.body: Shadows are black with transparency and a visible vertical offset; brand-colored glows and zero-offset halos do not belong in this system.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Rule
rules.body: Reduced motion keeps state, focus, and hierarchy visible while removing scroll animation, image scaling, lifts, and transition timing.

rules.name: The Motion Contrast Rule
rules.body: Scroll choreography never fades or filters text and controls that remain readable or interactive below WCAG AA at any intermediate frame.

rules.name: The Photo Provenance Rule
rules.body: Public convention-photo labels describe visible scenes year-neutrally unless a capture year is materially relevant and independently verified.

rules.name: The One Silhouette Rule
rules.body: Use the 8px surface family for cards, notices, forms, images, and dialogs; reserve circles and pills for controls whose compact function earns them.

dos: Do lead visitors from fee understanding to one form per attendee, then to the separate hotel step.
Do use the approved FCI tertiary logo, verified prior-convention imagery, and approved speaker and resort imagery at their natural aspect ratios.
Do keep instructional copy within the 65–75 character reading measure and maintain document-level reflow at every supported width.
Do keep direct-form fallbacks visible before cross-origin embeds and make loading, failure, retry, and no-JavaScript states truthful.
Do preserve 44px controls, visible focus, WCAG AA text contrast, and the reduced-motion alternative in every new component.
Do use responsive media candidates for routine views while retaining originals only when the lightbox or fallback requires them.
donts: Don't reconstruct the FCI mark with CSS, replace it with typed “FCI,” distort it, or place it on an unverified color treatment.
Don't present sponsorship as attendee registration or imply that the host page can verify a Jotform submission.
Don't use lime as ambient decoration, coral as normal-size text on light surfaces, or brand-colored shadows as depth.
Don't add autoplaying or eagerly loaded video; playback remains explicit, desktop-only, Save-Data-aware, and disabled for reduced motion.
Don't place essential fees, role choice, recovery, or hotel continuity behind decorative proof or a gallery.
Don't assign a capture year to convention photography from a filename, caption history, or assumption.
Don't introduce generic conference claims, fabricated testimonials, decorative icons, gradients in text, or a dark-mode contract without product approval.
